teaser.text: AutoZone is a retailer and distributor that helps drivers and repair shops keep cars and light trucks running. It makes money by selling the right products, then using the proceeds to operate the network that keeps those products available.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for AutoZone, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is $3,151.23 in October 2027 (+1%) and $3,778.88 in October 2029 (+21%). The forecast assigns 28% probability to bear, 52% to base, and 20% to bull. The next earnings release is expected around December 8, 2026, though unconfirmed; it will test DIY traffic stabilization and whether sales growth absorbs higher SG&A—the store, rent, and administrative costs. Through FY2027, Mega Hub-linked programs must deepen repeat sales and store cohorts approach management’s return curve. By FY2028 and FY2029, stronger free cash flow and international results support faster repurchases and the bull case; weak traffic, slow hub returns, or tighter financing push toward the bear case.

blocks.heading: How much cash does AutoZone really make?

paragraphs.text: Profit is not cash because accounting includes noncash items and timing differences. Stock compensation is also not an immediate cash payment, but employees receive shares that dilute existing owners. Subtracting stock pay therefore gives a stricter measure of what shareholders retain.

The trend matters more than one year’s total. Real free cash flow fell from fiscal 2022 to fiscal 2026 while capital spending rose. The company opened 374 stores in fiscal 2026 and continued building the infrastructure needed to improve parts availability and delivery speed. Those projects may support future sales, but the return must eventually catch up with the cash committed today.

blocks.heading: What has AutoZone guided for FY2027?

paragraphs.text: Management expects domestic same-store sales to be flat to up in the low single digits, with average ticket growth of about 4%. It expects commercial sales to grow at a high single-digit to low double-digit rate. International same-store sales are expected to grow in the low to mid-single digits on a constant-currency basis, which holds exchange rates steady so local demand is not confused with a weaker peso or real.

The cost plan is substantial. AutoZone expects roughly 400 store openings in FY2027 and about 3% growth in selling, general and administrative expenses per store. Total SG&A is expected to rise about 8%, before every new location has matured. The aging U.S. vehicle fleet supports the need for replacement parts, but management has not said how much transaction recovery is required or given an FY2027 EPS target. Those are the first gaps analysts must fill.

blocks.heading: What do AutoZone's last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: The fourth quarter ended more strongly, but it does not yet establish a durable recovery in underlying demand. Fiscal 2026’s fourth quarter covered 16 weeks, and revenue and operating results improved from the prior year.

blocks.heading: What should AutoZone watchers look for next?

paragraphs.text: The next earnings release is expected around December 8, 2026, though the date was not confirmed. Investors should look for ticket growth alongside stable transactions, and for sales growth that absorbs the planned SG&A increase. They should also watch whether commercial and new-store investment begins to improve productivity.
